writeup.headline: Janus Living rates Buy on strong quarterly revenue growth, but sits just one point above Hold.
writeup.thesis: Janus Living scores 65, exactly at the Buy edge, with the rating built on only three of six factors: growth, trend and news risk. Growth scores 99, driven by latest-quarter revenue growth of 45.4% year on year, with growth sped up by 10.9 pp from the previous quarter. Trend is weak at 36, with the price 8.1% below its 50-day average, 13.8% below its 52-week high, and shares 3.0 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. News risk is neutral at 50: two brokers trimmed price targets by $1 while keeping Overweight ratings, and no lawsuits, insider trades or guidance changes turned up in the window. Quality, balance sheet and valuation could not be scored, so the rating leans heavily on one strong growth quarter.
key_risks: The score is 1 point above Hold, so a small slip in any factor would cut the rating.
Weak share price trend: price 8.1% below its 50-day average and 3.9 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days.
Heavy dependence on Healthpeak as majority owner and external manager.
Q3 results due 2026-11-02 could show growth cooling from the latest-quarter rate of 45.4%.
Profitability, debt and valuation are unscored, so these possible weak spots are not reflected in the rating.
what_would_change: Down to Hold: a 1-point drop, such as a further weakening in trend or a negative news item around Q3 results.
Up to Strong Buy needs 15 more points, likely from a sustained trend recovery above the 50-day average and positive news such as another guidance raise.
Once quality, balance sheet and valuation can be scored, they could move the score materially in either direction.
